<!-- EDIT: say which rfr-fit job in this set this explains, and what question
     the importance and dependence plots are meant to answer. -->

Explains the forest the `rfr-fit` job in this set saved.

An `rfr-explain` job never grows a forest. It reads `rfr.rds`, which the fit
job writes. VIMP, minimal depth and the partial-dependence plots all describe
that saved forest and no other. Each expensive step is cached on its own:
changing how many variables get dependence plots recomputes the partials and
nothing else. For a variable screen and VarPro partials, use the `vp-fit` and
`vp-explain` jobs.

<!-- With `BANDS_B` above 0 the job also grows subsample forests, each on a fraction of the
     patients, to put confidence intervals on the importance and bands on the partial plots.
     It still grows no forest on the full cohort, and with `BANDS_B <- 0`, the default, it
     draws neither. -->

<!-- The two values below are written by add_job() from the subject/type it
     was called with, which are also the filename's first two fields. They
     name the SET this job belongs to, and every artifact path in the
     document is computed from them, so no output path below needs editing.

     Do NOT hand-edit these declarations: the render-time guard below checks
     them against this file's own name and stops if they disagree. To put
     this job in a different set, call add_job() again with the new
     subject/type rather than editing this copy in place.

     A set is keyed on (subject, analysis type), not on the subject alone.
     One subject may be analyzed by several methods -- parametric hazard, random
     forest survival, competing risks -- and those chains share their upstream.
     Two sets keyed on `dead_pa` alone would write their life tables to the
     same file. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
SUBJECT <- "los"
TYPE    <- "rfr"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(randomForestSRC)
  library(ggRandomForests)
  library(hvtiRutilities)
})
# One thread, so a forest reproduces from machine to machine. Left unset,
# randomForestSRC runs on every core its OpenMP build can see, and on a
# multi-core server a varPro cross-validated cutoff changed with the thread
# count with every seed held fixed. Raise it for speed on a large forest, at the
# cost of that guarantee: a cached fit records its seed, data and package
# versions, never the threads it ran on.
options(rf.cores = 1L)
# The versions this template was verified against, end to end, on 2026-09-19.
# Below them a call here can fail or change meaning, and the message would
# arrive mid-render rather than here.
if (utils::packageVersion("randomForestSRC") < "3.7.0") {
  stop("This job needs randomForestSRC >= 3.7.0; ", utils::packageVersion("randomForestSRC"),
       " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (utils::packageVersion("ggRandomForests") < "4.0.0") {
  stop("This job needs ggRandomForests >= 4.0.0; ", utils::packageVersion("ggRandomForests"),
       " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
# The study root is the nearest directory above this file holding _study.yml,
# so the job renders the same from the Render button, quarto render, or
# render_job(), at any depth, with no path in this document to edit.
# Without the guard in .job_setup(), an unedited job renders green over a
# meaningless analysis. Here that is dependence plots for a placeholder number
# of variables, which look exactly like a result.
# To render a job you have not finished, leave a chunk out with the chunk
# option skip, giving the reason in quotes, or call hvtiRtemplates::stop_here()
# in a chunk to leave out everything below it. A draft lists each one in a
# callout; a final render refuses them, as it refuses an unresolved marker.
# ?stop_here has more.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment())
.root <- .job$root
set_path <- .job$set_path
.provenance_data <- list()
# Saves a figure as <name>.png, .pdf and .tiff in this set's graphs/ folder (or `kind`'s),
# under the SAVE_FIGURES and FIGURES study choices.
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width = 6, height = 4, kind = "graphs", linked = FALSE) {
  hvtiRtemplates:::.save_figure(plot, set_path(kind, paste0(name, ".png")), width, height,
                                SAVE_FIGURES, FIGURES, linked)
}

# `rfr-explain` reads the forest `rfr-fit` wrote in this same set, and caches
# its own work beside it.
# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Study choices

Edit these values for this study before rendering. The outcome and predictors
are not here: they come from the forest.

```{r}
#| label: edit-study-choices
# EDIT: the fit's selection is used; set any of these only to confirm it.
# NULL takes the value the fit job used.
WHERE <- NULL
ID <- NULL
KEY <- NULL

# EDIT: how many variables get dependence plots, ranked by VIMP. The partials
# are the expensive step, so keep this small.
# With BANDS_B above 0, a bigger TOP_K computes bands only for the new variables, but
# still regrows all BANDS_B subsample forests to do it.
TOP_K <- 8

# EDIT: or name the variables yourself. NULL takes the top TOP_K by VIMP.
PARTIAL_VARS <- NULL

# EDIT: seed for VIMP and the partials. It is part of every cache key.
# cache_fit() seeds R's generator with it before each call, and vimp() is also
# handed it as `seed =`, negated as randomForestSRC documents.
SEED <- 2026

# EDIT: subsample forests for the confidence intervals on importance and the
# bands on the partial plots. 0 draws neither.
#   25-50 for a first look at a draft; the bands are rough but show their shape.
#   100 for a report. It is randomForestSRC's default, and enough because the
#   intervals are estimate +/- 1.96 SE: they need a stable SE, not stable tail
#   percentiles, which would take several hundred.
#   200 or more only for 99% intervals, or when a rerun with another SEED moves
#   the band edges by more than you would accept in a figure.
# Cost is about BANDS_B x SUBRATIO fits of the full forest. Submit the job to
# compute them; job_status() shows how many forests are grown and the time left.
BANDS_B <- 0

# EDIT: fraction of patients in each subsample. NULL takes randomForestSRC's
# default, exp(-1) (0.37) up to 1000 patients and exp(-1) * sqrt(1000 / n) above,
# so a larger cohort gets a smaller fraction. Leave it NULL unless you have a
# reason to change it.
#   Small subsamples grow shallow forests whose curves are flatter than the full
#   forest's.
#   Keep it at or below 0.5. Subsampling estimates the spread only while each
#   subsample is a small part of the cohort; near 1 every subsample forest is
#   nearly the full forest, and the bands shrink to the forest's own tree-to-tree
#   noise, far narrower than the real uncertainty.
SUBRATIO <- NULL

# EDIT: how the partial plots draw their bands. "ribbon" shades a band around
# each continuous curve; "bars" draws an error bar at each grid point instead,
# which reads better in black and white. Categorical predictors always get error bars.
BAND_STYLE <- "ribbon"

# EDIT: with BAND_STYLE <- "bars", where to draw the bars, as a named list of
# values per continuous predictor, e.g. list(age = c(50, 60, 70, 80), lvef = c(30, 50)).
# NULL, or a predictor left out, draws a bar at every grid point. The values
# must lie inside the range of the predictor's partial plot, which can be
# narrower than its observed range; the job stops before growing anything if one
# does not. Changing them only redraws: each subsample curve is read off at
# these values the way the plotted line is drawn, straight between grid points,
# so no forest is regrown.
BAND_AT <- NULL

# Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the
# render instead of returning the old result; TRUE recomputes only the caches
# that are out of date.
REFIT <- FALSE

# Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word), and a PDF and a TIFF (for the publisher).
# SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names
# start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("hp-survival"). The names are the
# file names, listed for each template in the templates README.
SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE
FIGURES <- NULL
```

## The forest

```{r}
#| label: forest
.handoff <- set_path("estimates", "rfr.rds")
if (!file.exists(.handoff)) {
  stop("No forest at ", .handoff, ". Render the rfr-fit job in this set first; ",
       "this job explains that forest and never grows its own.", call. = FALSE)
}
.cfg <- study_config(start = .root)
.forest_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.handoff, "forest", .cfg, "the rfr-fit job")
forest <- .forest_read$value
.provenance_data <- .forest_read$lineage$data
.provenance_artifacts <- c(.forest_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.forest_read$record))
if (!identical(forest$family, "regr")) {
  stop("rfr.rds holds a '", forest$family, "' forest, not a regression forest.", call. = FALSE)
}
CACHE_DIR <- dirname(.handoff)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "The data the fit job read"
# This job reads no data: the forest carries its training rows. The fit job
# recorded how it chose them, and a setting above that differs from the fit's
# stops here rather than describe rows the forest was not grown on.
.sel <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_upstream_job_data(
  .cfg, .forest_read$lineage, list(where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY), read = FALSE, source = "rfr.rds"
)$selection
knitr::kable(data.frame(step = c("ID", "KEY", "WHERE", "Rows"),
                        value = c(.sel$id, paste(.sel$key, collapse = ", "),
                                  if (length(.sel$where_shown)) paste(.sel$where_shown, collapse = "; ") else "none",
                                  .sel$rows)),
             col.names = c("Data", ""))
```

## Importance

```{r}
#| label: fig-importance
#| fig-cap: "VIMP (anti-split importance) of each predictor. Horizontal bars give the importance of each predictor, in one
#|   color where the importance is positive and another where it is not, as in the legend."
#| fig-height: 10.5
#| message: true
vi <- cache_fit("rfr-vimp", vimp(forest, seed = -abs(SEED)), seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT)
# Free size: one row per predictor, so the height grows with the list.
# The manuscript theme hides the legend and its title, and the caption reads the colors from the legend.
.fig <- plot(gg_vimp(vi)) +
  hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top", legend.title = ggplot2::element_text())
save_figure(.fig, "rfr-explain-importance", height = 7)
.fig
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-importance
#| tbl-cap: "VIMP (anti-split importance) and minimal depth of each predictor, in order of importance"
# Minimal depth ranks by how near the root a variable first splits, a second
# opinion that needs no VIMP calculation. Cheap, so not cached.
ranked <- names(sort(vi$importance, decreasing = TRUE))
depth <- max.subtree(forest)$order[, 1]
data.frame(variable = ranked,
           vimp = round(vi$importance[ranked], 4),
           min_depth = round(depth[ranked], 2),
           row.names = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: select
if (is.null(PARTIAL_VARS)) {
  sel <- head(ranked, TOP_K)
} else {
  # A misspelt name would otherwise fail deep inside the partial call, or be
  # dropped from a plot without a word.
  .unknown <- setdiff(PARTIAL_VARS, forest$xvar.names)
  if (length(.unknown)) {
    stop("PARTIAL_VARS names variable(s) the forest was not grown on: ",
         paste(.unknown, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  sel <- PARTIAL_VARS
}
# Each dependence figure is drawn a page at a time, panels in a grid no larger
# than the printed page (6.5 by 9 in), and each page is a child chunk of its
# own so Quarto numbers it, as dc-eda's pages are. A study's TOP_K or
# PARTIAL_VARS sets how many pages there are; nothing here refuses a count.
.fence <- strrep("`", 3)
.page_child <- function(kind, i, pages, vars, caption) {
  page <- pages[[i]]
  if (length(pages) > 1L) {
    caption <- paste0(caption, " Page ", i, " of ", length(pages), ": ",
                      paste(vars[page$index], collapse = ", "), ".")
  }
  code <- c(paste0(.fence, "{r}"), paste0("#| label: fig-", kind, "-", i),
            paste0("#| fig-cap: ", encodeString(caption, quote = "\"")),
            sprintf("#| fig-width: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(page$width)),
            sprintf("#| fig-height: %g", hvtiRtemplates:::.report_size(page$height)), ".fig", .fence)
  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = code, envir = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

## Dependence

```{r}
#| label: dependence-marginal
#| results: asis
#| message: true
# unnumbered: each page below is a child chunk with its own label and caption
# Marginal: predicted outcome against each variable, as observed.
# A loess smooth needs more than a handful of distinct values, so a predictor
# with fewer than six, such as a stage or a grade, is drawn as points alone.
.gv <- gg_variable(forest)
.panels <- lapply(sel, function(v) {
  plot(.gv, xvar = v, smooth = length(unique(stats::na.omit(.gv[[v]]))) > 5) +
    hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
})
.cap <- paste("Predicted outcome against each selected predictor, as observed, one panel per predictor.",
              "Black filled circles are individual patients and the blue line a loess smooth with its gray",
              "band, drawn for predictors with more than five distinct values; for a categorical predictor",
              "the points are jittered over a gray box plot.")
# Free size, paged: one panel per predictor.
.pages <- hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(sel), panel_width = 3.25, panel_height = 2.5)
for (.i in seq_along(.pages)) {
  .fig <- patchwork::wrap_plots(.panels[.pages[[.i]]$index], ncol = .pages[[.i]]$ncol)
  save_figure(.fig, sprintf("rfr-explain-dependence-marginal-page-%02d", .i),
              width = .pages[[.i]]$width, height = .pages[[.i]]$height)
  .page_child("dependence-marginal", .i, .pages, sel, .cap)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: dependence-partial
#| results: asis
#| message: true
# unnumbered: each page below is a child chunk with its own label and caption
# Partial: the forest's prediction with every other variable held at its
# observed values.
pd <- cache_fit("rfr-partial", gg_partial_rfsrc(forest, xvar.names = sel),
                seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                packages = "randomForestSRC")
.cap <- paste("Partial dependence of the forest's prediction on each selected predictor, one panel per",
              "predictor. Black solid lines trace the partial effect across a continuous predictor, and",
              "dark gray bars give it at each level of a categorical one.")
# Free size, paged: one facet per predictor, two by two.
.pages <- hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(sel), panel_width = 3.25, panel_height = 3, page_height = 6)
for (.i in seq_along(.pages)) {
  .vars <- sel[.pages[[.i]]$index]
  .fig <- plot(hvtiRtemplates:::.partial_subset(pd, .vars)) &
    hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12)
  save_figure(.fig, sprintf("rfr-explain-dependence-partial-page-%02d", .i),
              width = .pages[[.i]]$width, height = .pages[[.i]]$height)
  .page_child("dependence-partial", .i, .pages, sel, .cap)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: bands-plan
#| include: !expr 'BANDS_B > 0'
#| results: asis
# Checks the band choices before anything is grown, and says what will be. With BANDS_B at 0 it
# writes nothing, so the job renders as it did before the bands existed.
# unnumbered: a three-row summary of the band settings, not a result the report cites
if (BANDS_B > 0) {
  cat("## Confidence bands\n\n")
  cat(paste(
    "Each subsample forest is grown on a fraction of the patients, and the intervals are",
    "the full forest's value plus and minus 1.96 jackknife standard errors (Ishwaran and Lu, 2019). They are",
    "pointwise: each bounds the curve at one value, not the whole curve."
  ), "\n\n", sep = "")
  .bands <- hvtiRtemplates:::.band_plan(forest, BANDS_B, SUBRATIO, BAND_STYLE, BAND_AT, sel, pd)
  .subratio <- .bands$subratio
  print(knitr::kable(.bands$table, col.names = c("Confidence bands", "")))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: importance-intervals
#| include: !expr 'BANDS_B > 0'
#| results: asis
#| message: true
# unnumbered: the figure below is a child chunk with its own label and caption
if (BANDS_B > 0) {
  # The subsample forests give the standard error. "anti" is the importance vimp() computed for the
  # figure above. Only the VIMP of each subsample forest is cached, one column per subsample: the whole
  # subsample() object carries a forest, and the SE needs nothing else. Quoted once, so the check below
  # and cache_fit() read the same call.
  .ci_code <- quote(hvtiRtemplates:::.band_vimp_star(subsample(forest, B = BANDS_B, subratio = .subratio,
                                                               importance = "anti", verbose = FALSE)))
  # Refused at the console only when the intervals will actually be computed: a current
  # cache loads, even under REFIT.
  if (hvtiRutilities::cache_would_fit("rfr-vimp-subsample", .ci_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                                      packages = "randomForestSRC")) {
    hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit("rfr-vimp-subsample", dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                                   why = sprintf("the importance intervals regrow the forest %d times", BANDS_B))
  }
  vi_star <- cache_fit("rfr-vimp-subsample", .ci_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                       packages = "randomForestSRC")
  # The points are the importance figure's own estimate, so the two figures cannot disagree in sign or
  # order. The SE is taken about that same estimate: the spread of the subsample forests' VIMP around it,
  # scaled by the subsample fraction (the delete-d jackknife). subsample() reports its own SE about the VIMP
  # of its internal full forest, a different draw from the figure's, so it is not used.
  .vi_est <- vi$importance
  .fig <- hvtiRtemplates:::.plot_vimp_intervals(.vi_est, hvtiRtemplates:::.band_vimp_se(.vi_est, vi_star, .subratio)) +
    hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top")
  save_figure(.fig, "rfr-explain-importance-intervals", height = 7)
  .cap <- sprintf(paste("VIMP (anti-split importance) of each predictor, as in the importance figure, with a",
                        "pointwise 95%% interval of plus and minus 1.96 jackknife standard errors, taken about that",
                        "importance, from %d subsample forests, each grown on %.0f%% of patients. Points give the importance and",
                        "bars the interval, black where the interval lies above zero and gray where it does",
                        "not, as in the legend; the dashed line marks zero."), BANDS_B, 100 * .subratio)
  .page_child("importance-intervals", 1L, list(list(index = 1L, width = 6, height = 7)), "", .cap)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: dependence-partial-bands
#| include: !expr 'BANDS_B > 0'
#| results: asis
#| message: true
# unnumbered: each page below is a child chunk with its own label and caption
if (BANDS_B > 0) {
  .rows <- cache_fit("rfr-band-rows", hvtiRtemplates:::.band_rows(forest, BANDS_B, .subratio),
                     seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT)
  .grids <- lapply(stats::setNames(sel, sel), function(v) hvtiRtemplates:::.band_grid(pd, v))
  .times <- hvtiRtemplates:::.band_times(pd)
  # One band per variable, keyed on that variable's grid alone (.g), so a bigger TOP_K
  # leaves the bands already cached current. get() keeps the pool out of the key: it
  # changes with which variables still need a band.
  .band_code <- quote(hvtiRtemplates:::.band_partial(get(".pool"), forest, .rows, .v, .g, .times, SEED))
  # The variables whose band will be computed: no cache, or a stale one under REFIT. A
  # current cache loads even under REFIT, which a bigger TOP_K needs for the partials above.
  .todo <- character()
  for (.v in sel) {
    .g <- .grids[[.v]]
    if (hvtiRutilities::cache_would_fit(paste0("rfr-partial-band-", .v), .band_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR,
                                        refit = REFIT, packages = "randomForestSRC")) .todo <- c(.todo, .v)
  }
  if (length(.todo)) {
    hvtiRtemplates::guard_long_fit(paste0("rfr-partial-band-", .todo), dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT,
                                   why = sprintf("the partial-dependence bands regrow the forest %d times", BANDS_B))
  }
  # Reports each subsample forest to <job>.run.progress and the render log.
  .pool <- hvtiRtemplates:::.band_pool(.todo, .grids[.todo], progress = .job$progress("subsample forest"))
  bands <- list()
  for (.v in sel) {
    .g <- .grids[[.v]]
    bands[[.v]] <- cache_fit(paste0("rfr-partial-band-", .v), .band_code, seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR,
                             refit = REFIT, packages = "randomForestSRC")
  }
  .drawn <- if (identical(BAND_STYLE, "bars")) "error bars" else "shaded bands"
  .cap <- sprintf(paste("Partial dependence of the forest's prediction on each selected predictor, one panel",
                        "per predictor, with pointwise 95%% intervals from %d subsample forests, each grown on",
                        "%.0f%% of patients. Lines trace the predicted outcome across a continuous predictor with",
                        "%s around it, and points with error bars give it at each level of a categorical one."),
                  BANDS_B, 100 * .subratio, .drawn)
  .pages <- hvtiRtemplates:::.figure_pages(length(sel), panel_width = 3.25, panel_height = 3, page_height = 6)
  for (.i in seq_along(.pages)) {
    .vars <- sel[.pages[[.i]]$index]
    .fig <- hvtiRtemplates:::.plot_partial_bands(bands[.vars], .subratio, BAND_STYLE, BAND_AT,
                                                 ncol = .pages[[.i]]$ncol) &
      hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12, legend.position = "top",
                                     legend.title = ggplot2::element_text())
    save_figure(.fig, sprintf("rfr-explain-dependence-partial-bands-page-%02d", .i),
                width = .pages[[.i]]$width, height = .pages[[.i]]$height)
    .page_child("dependence-partial-bands", .i, .pages, sel, .cap)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: provenance

cat(hvtiRtemplates:::.embed_provenance(
  .in,
  data = .provenance_data,
  run = .job$run,
  artifacts = .provenance_artifacts,
  extra = list(
```
